fact_text: Ipak is a Pakistani flexible packaging film maker; management said its films are used in about 90% of food packaging, a claim the reporter presented without independent check.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak entered the flexible packaging industry in 2010 as a converter, buying film from the market's one main supplier.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Until 2014 Ipak depended on the single main film supplier in its market, and supply issues and that supplier's capacity limits led to back-and-forth problems.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: In 2014 Ipak decided to build its own film line as a greenfield project rather than a standard backward integration, because film making is far larger in scale and capital intensity than converting.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: A government tax benefit for a 100% self-financed greenfield project, available for five years at the time, was part of the basis for Ipak's 2014 film line decision, which shareholders approved.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak announced its film manufacturing investment in the first quarter of 2015.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak's film plant started commercial operation on 14 August 2017.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: After COVID, Ipak announced a major expansion: a second, more efficient and specialised film line added to its existing line range.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak added a BOPP film business alongside its polymer film lines, a material the reporter noted is used largely in food packaging.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Management said Ipak is the only one-window supplier in its market offering the full range of flexible packaging film segments.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak's film line co-extrudes five layers: four extruders and one main extruder feed a die, forming a single molten sheet that is quenched in a water bath, dried and passed on for stretching.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak stretches its film in the machine and transverse directions to about 5.5 to 5.8 times, depending on film type, to improve mechanical properties.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Stretching matters because customers' high-speed printing machines run at about 450 to 500 metres, and a film with weak mechanical properties cannot perform on them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak winds its film into jumbo rolls of about 10.4 m and 8.7 m on different lines, then slits them to each customer's specified widths before packing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak metallises film by depositing 99.99% pure aluminium in a closed vacuum chamber at high speed, giving light, water vapour, oxygen and aroma barriers and turning the film opaque silver.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: A printed and metallised two-layer laminate must be checked for whether the metal or the print lifts off at the bond, a functional property the process tests.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: In one example, a packed snack lost its crispness after three months, against a six-month target shelf life, which is why functional tests check shelf life.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak's product development starts from the customer's brief, then packs samples held for three, four or six months to test shelf life and logistics before final approval and locking the specification.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Management said Ipak controls quality across raw material, extrusion, casting, cooling, orientation and winding, using protocols meant to match tests run in any international lab.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak regrinds its off-grade film in in-house recycling machines back into granules, so that its production waste is reused.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Management claimed Ipak is the only Pakistani company exporting recycling-based film, and that it is the largest film maker in the country by market share.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: In 2024 Ipak reset its vision from a commodity film exporter toward a specialised global flexible packaging leader, backed by its own product development and technical services.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Ipak's management said its plan is to be a global specialised leader in flexible packaging by 2030.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Management argued that a specialised supplier gets closer customer ties, because customers bring it product and machine problems, unlike commodity film sold on price.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)

fact_text: Management said its customers in Japan focus on sustainability, thinner wrappers, plastic reduction and longer shelf life rather than commodity film discussion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Inside IPAK: The packaging firm that powers everyday brands | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-27)
